definition: unable to pay one's debts, and legally declared so
hook: Going bankrupt used to involve someone smashing furniture in public.
modernAnchor: A boarded-up shop. A court filing. A business that ran out of money. We call it bankrupt.
journey: Italian moneylenders did business at a bench in the marketplace. The bench was the banca, and it gave us the word bank.
A lender who could not repay his customers lost his place in the market.
Tradition says the crowd broke his bench in public, banca rotta, so everyone knew he was finished.
French and then English borrowed the phrase, and the broken bench became a legal state.
